title: Dynamic interleaved stage allocator to reduce inter-GPU stalls for prefill/decode
creator: Maya Chen
description: Reduce end-to-end latency and tail variance during prefill+decode on heterogeneous multi-GPU boxes by implementing a Dynamic Interleaved Stage Allocator (DISA). DISA opportunistically shifts prefill microbatches and decode tokens across tensor/pipeline stages to create communication windows that overlap with compute, avoid global barriers, and enable better kernel choices for attention tiling. The feature must be compatible with current token-prefill cache, model sharding, and model-variant fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: 10-30% mean latency improvement on representative GPT-like prefills across internal benchmark suite with <=5% p95 regression for short-context requests
Demonstrated NCCL allreduce/alltoall overlap for >70% of microbatch windows on test topology (4xA100-same-rack) without increasing GPU memory beyond 5%
Fallback to conservative allocator when model pins or KVM constraints are present and no functional regressions observed
Unit and integration tests covering stage reallocation, soft-rendezvous, and kernel-selection hooks merged
Perf dashboard with per-stage latency, NCCL overlap %, and kernel selection counters available in Console release runtime-1.20
tasks: Design spec: define state machine for interleaved allocation and soft-rendezvous points
Instrument runtime: add per-stage timing probes and comm-window markers
Scheduler: implement heuristic that aligns microbatch start offsets to create non-blocking NCCL windows
Kernel selection hook: expose stage-local sequence-length distribution to kernel selector
Sim tests: create synthetic prefill/decode traces to validate overlap behavior under varying seq-len and batch sizes
Safety: implement conservative fallbacks and per-tenant toggles
Perf validation: run CI artifacts across topology matrix and push dashboard metrics
decisions: Prefer soft-rendezvous (relaxed per-stage alignment) over global barriers to avoid tail amplification for mixed request lengths
Initial heuristic uses token-stripe alignment + microbatch skew up to 3 microbatches; will expand to learned policy in follow-up
Kernel selection will be augmented with a lightweight histogram of local sequence lengths (rolling N=256) rather than full trace shipping to central planner
Do not change persistent KV cache layout; DISA only shifts runtime microbatch timing to preserve cache hit semantics

When to migrate DISA to a learning-based policy vs keeping heuristic-based approach?
